name: C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 4

function.text: CXCR4 encodes C-X-C chemokine receptor type 4. Annotated molecular activities include coreceptor activity and virus receptor activity. It participates in neurogenesis and apoptotic process.

germline.text: Strong or definitive GenCC assertions link constitutional variants to WHIM syndrome (autosomal dominant); WHIM syndrome 1 (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Reported somatic alteration contexts include Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma. The alteration class and exact variant must be assessed in the disease context.

function.text: CXCR4 encodes C-X-C chemokine receptor type 4. Based in part on similarity, it is a receptor for the C-X-C chemokine CXCL12/SDF-1 that transduces a signal by increasing intracellular calcium ion levels and enhancing MAPK1/MAPK3 activation. CXCR4 is coupled to G(i) G alpha proteins and mediates inhibition of adenylate cyclase. It participates in the AKT signaling cascade.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with WHIM syndrome (autosomal dominant); WHIM syndrome 1 (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving CXCR4 have been reported in lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma.
